pictureAnalogies.why: A sock goes on a foot, so a glove goes on a hand.
A cow gives us milk, so a chicken gives us eggs.
A fish lives in the water, so a bird belongs in the sky.
Ice is cold, so fire is hot.
A teacher works at a school, so a doctor works at a hospital.
A car drives on a road, so a train runs on tracks.
You put on a coat when it is cold, so you take an umbrella when it rains.
You use scissors on paper, so you use a spoon for soup.
A chick grows up into a chicken, so a caterpillar grows up into a butterfly.
A leaf is one part of a tree, so a page is one part of a book.
A cap goes on your head, so glasses go over your eyes.
You read a book, so you listen to a song.
A bee makes honey, so a sheep gives us wool.
A key is used on a door, so a hammer is used on a nail.
You sleep at night, so you wake up in the morning.
An elephant is big and a mouse is small, so next to a tall tree a tiny seedling is the small one.
An egg grows into a chick, so a seed grows into a flower.
Wheat is made into bread, so milk is made into cheese.
An airplane travels through the sky, so a boat travels on the water.
You put mittens on in the snow, so you put sunglasses on in the sun.
A bee feeds at a flower, so a cow feeds on grass.
A fire engine is sent to a fire, so an ambulance is sent to someone who is sick.
A toothbrush cleans your teeth, so soap cleans your hands.
A paintbrush is used with paint, so a pencil is used on paper.
A ring goes on a finger, so a watch goes on your arm.
Bread is made into a sandwich, so potatoes are made into fries.
A dog likes to chew a bone, so a cat likes to eat a fish.
A fish lives in the ocean, so a camel lives in the desert.
A chef works with a pan, so a farmer works with a tractor.
A guitar makes music, so a crayon makes a picture.
You kick a soccer ball with your foot, so you throw a basketball with your hands.
A bucket holds water, so a basket holds apples.
A rabbit eats carrots, so a koala eats leaves.
A suitcase carries clothes, so a backpack carries books.
A rooster calls in the morning, so an owl is awake at night.
A flashlight runs on a battery, so a car runs on gas.
A firefighter drives a fire engine, so a police officer drives a police car.
Honey comes from a bee, so an egg comes from a chicken.
A nest is a bird's home, so a web is a spider's home.
A monkey eats bananas, so a panda eats bamboo.
A school bus takes you to school, so an ambulance takes you to the hospital.
Apples are baked into pie, so milk is frozen into ice cream.
A sock goes on before a shoe, so a shirt goes on before a jacket.
A plant needs water to grow, so a fire needs wood to burn.

pictureGroups.why: They are all animals.
They are all fruit. A carrot is a vegetable.
They are all clothes you wear.
They are all things you see in the sky.
They all carry people from place to place. A bird moves, but nobody rides one.
They are all food.
They are all things you make marks with.
They are all flowers. A tree is a plant, but it is not a flower.
They are all tools for building and fixing.
They are all vegetables.
They are all balls, and a ball is round.
They all live in the ocean.
They are all buildings people go to.
They are all insects. A spider is not an insect — it has eight legs.
They are all odd numbers — they cannot be split into two equal groups.
They can all fly.
They are all fruit you peel or squeeze.
They all carry many people at once.
They all go on your feet.
They are all things you set on a table to eat with.
They are all kinds of weather.
They are all insects — they all have six legs.
They are all parts of the body you sense with.
They are all instruments that make music.
They all give off light.
They all come to help in an emergency.
They are all large land animals.
They are all used to build things.
They are all things you put on to keep warm.
They can all swim in water.
They are all things with words to read.
They are all foods you keep in a kitchen.
They all tell you about time.
They are all plants that grow.
They are all places someone can live in.
They are all parts of keeping a house shut or open.
They are all sweet things to eat.
You can see them all up in the sky.
They all have wheels and carry one person.
They are all animals that live on a farm.

sentenceCompletion.s: You wear shoes on your ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Shoes are made to fit feet.

sentenceCompletion.s: We eat soup with a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A spoon holds liquid; a fork lets it run through.

sentenceCompletion.s: A fish swims in the ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A fish breathes underwater, so water is the only place it can live.

sentenceCompletion.s: At night you sleep in a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A bed is the thing in a house made for sleeping.

sentenceCompletion.s: You write your name with a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A pencil is the one that makes marks on paper.

sentenceCompletion.s: You use your ___ to hear a song.
sentenceCompletion.why: Each part of the body has its own job, and ears do the hearing.

sentenceCompletion.s: A cow gives us ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Eggs come from chickens and honey from bees, but milk comes from a cow.

sentenceCompletion.s: When it rains you open an ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: An umbrella keeps the rain off you; sunglasses are for a bright day.

sentenceCompletion.s: You open a door with a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A key is the one shaped to fit a lock.

sentenceCompletion.s: Every morning you brush your ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Brushing keeps teeth clean. You wash the rest of you a different way.

sentenceCompletion.s: A bird builds a ___ to live in.
sentenceCompletion.why: Birds gather twigs and grass to make a nest.

sentenceCompletion.s: A bee makes ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey.

sentenceCompletion.s: A caterpillar turns into a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A caterpillar changes shape as it grows up, and it becomes a butterfly.

sentenceCompletion.s: A doctor takes care of people at the ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A teacher works at a school and a doctor works at a hospital.

sentenceCompletion.s: To send a letter you put it in the ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A letter has to go somewhere a mail carrier will collect it.

sentenceCompletion.s: When it snows outside you put on a warm ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A coat holds your heat in. A t-shirt and shorts are for a hot day.

sentenceCompletion.s: A bee lands on a ___ to find nectar.
sentenceCompletion.why: Flowers hold the nectar bees gather.

sentenceCompletion.s: You cut paper with a pair of ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Scissors have two blades that slice through paper.

sentenceCompletion.s: A farmer drives a ___ in the field.
sentenceCompletion.why: A tractor is built to pull heavy loads over soft ground.

sentenceCompletion.s: When you are thirsty you drink a glass of ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Only one of these is something you can drink.

sentenceCompletion.s: A spider spins a ___ to catch its food.
sentenceCompletion.why: The sticky threads of a web trap insects.

sentenceCompletion.s: You keep your feet warm in winter with thick ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Socks cover your feet; glasses go over your eyes.

sentenceCompletion.s: A baby drinks milk from a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A bottle is made for a baby who cannot hold a cup yet.

sentenceCompletion.s: You carry water from the tap in a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A bucket holds water; the others would let it run straight out.

sentenceCompletion.s: When the sun is bright you wear ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Sunglasses shade your eyes. Mittens and scarves are for cold days.

sentenceCompletion.s: A cat likes to chase a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Cats hunt small animals like mice.

sentenceCompletion.s: You wash your hands with water and ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Soap lifts the dirt off your skin so water can rinse it away.

sentenceCompletion.s: A bird sits on its eggs up in a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A nest is where a bird keeps its eggs safe.

sentenceCompletion.s: A duck swims on the ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Ducks are water birds, so they swim where there is water.

sentenceCompletion.s: You look at the time on a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A clock is the thing made to show the time.

sentenceCompletion.s: A bear sleeps all winter inside a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A cave is a big sheltered space where a bear can rest.

sentenceCompletion.s: You cool a drink down by adding ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Ice is frozen, so it takes the heat out of a drink.

sentenceCompletion.s: A butterfly rests on a ___ in the garden.
sentenceCompletion.why: Butterflies feed at flowers.

sentenceCompletion.s: A firefighter puts out a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Putting out fires is a firefighter's job.

sentenceCompletion.s: You cover your head in the rain with an ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: An umbrella keeps the rain off.

sentenceCompletion.s: An ant is very ___ next to an elephant.
sentenceCompletion.why: Next to the largest land animal, an ant is tiny.

sentenceCompletion.s: A horse pulls a heavy ___ down the road.
sentenceCompletion.why: A horse is strong enough to pull something heavy.

sentenceCompletion.s: You carry your books to school in a ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: A backpack is made for carrying things on your back.

sentenceCompletion.s: A snail carries its ___ on its back.
sentenceCompletion.why: A snail's shell is its home and it goes everywhere with it.

sentenceCompletion.s: At a birthday party you blow out the ___.
sentenceCompletion.why: Candles are what you blow out on a birthday cake.
